model.name: Meeting / Session
model.purpose: Provide the context an agent needs to convene, run, observe and hand off a single meeting or session occurrence — identity, convening basis, timing, setting, participation, agenda, conduct, outcomes and record obligations — without owning the durable records, the convening body or the parties it references.
model.scope_statement: WM-ACT-025 models one bounded occurrence in which two or more parties are convened, synchronously or in mixed mode, to transact business under a shared agenda. It covers the occurrence from convocation to close: how it is identified and classified, on whose authority it was called, when and where it takes place, who was invited and who was actually present, what was on the agenda, what procedural acts and votes occurred, what outcomes were reached, what was captured during the session, how open the session was, and which durable records it owes. It deliberately stops at the boundary of the artefacts it produces and the actors it references: minutes and transcripts (WM-REC-012), decision records (WM-REC-010), the convening body (WM-ORG-018), parties, places, tasks and documents are referenced with subject-specific binding parameters only. The model is storage- and interface-neutral; iCalendar, JSCalendar, schema.org, XCON and vendor conferencing objects are alignments and projections, not the semantics.
in_scope: Identity, classification and revision of a single meeting or session occurrence, including its position in a recurring series.
Binding to the convening authority and the convocation notice, with the sufficiency tests attached to that notice.
Planned and observed timing, suspension and resumption, rescheduling, postponement and cancellation of the occurrence.
Physical setting, virtual conferencing endpoints, mixed-mode equivalence, reserved resources and accessibility provision.
Invited and actual participation: roles, invitation response state, delegation and proxy, presence observation and recusal.
Quorum determination at this occurrence, measured against a threshold rule owned by the convening body.
Agenda composition, adoption, amendment, deferral and carry-over, with references to tabled papers.
Conduct of proceedings: procedural acts, speaking-turn management, motions, voting method, tally and declared result.
Outcomes reached and follow-up assignments, expressed as references to the records and tasks that carry them.
In-session capture (recording, live transcription) with notification and consent basis, and the obligation to produce durable records.
Openness and closure of the session or its portions, observer admission, and the inventory of session-held personal data.
Declarative alignment to calendar, event and conferencing vocabularies.
out_of_scope: Drafting, approval, authenticity, publication and disposition of the minutes or transcript — owned by WM-REC-012; 'approval of the minutes' appears here only as an agenda item of a later session.
Content, status, rationale, supersession and implementation tracking of decision records — owned by WM-REC-010.
Composition, mandate, terms of reference, standing membership, chair designation rules and delegated powers of the convening body — owned by WM-ORG-018.
Master identity, contact data and affiliation of persons and organisations — owned by the adopting Dimension's party models.
Master data for places, buildings and rooms — only the reference and a local room designation are held here.
Generic occurrence semantics shared by all activities — owned by the parent model WM-ACT-018.
Execution and completion lifecycle of assigned actions — owned by the task model.
Version and custody management of tabled papers — owned by the document model.
Runtime evaluation and enforcement of access decisions, and storage of audit trails; this model carries classifications and references to audit events only.
Operation of calendaring transport (iTIP, CalDAV) and conferencing media transport, floor-control protocol mechanics and codec negotiation.
Decisions taken without a meeting (written resolutions, silence or written procedure) where no session occurrence exists.
Meeting-effectiveness analytics, sentiment scoring and engagement metrics.

boundary_notes.distinction: This model records that a record is owed, which content the applicable regime requires, who must produce and certify it, and which agenda item each passage anchors to. The record's own draft, approval, correction, authenticity and disposition lifecycle belongs to WM-REC-012.

Putting a question, the voting method, the tally and the declaration of the result are session conduct and are modelled here. The durable decision with its rationale, status, supersession and implementation is carried by WM-REC-010 and referenced by identifier.

Quorum thresholds, membership, voting entitlement and delegated powers are properties of the body's constitution. This model records only the determination made at this occurrence and the officer who presided over it.

Generic occurrence identity, scheduling status and cancellation semantics common to all activities are inherited from the parent. This model specialises only the deliberative surface: agenda, quorum, motions, capture and record obligation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party models for persons and organisations
boundary_notes.distinction: Participants are references. Role, invitation response, presence intervals and recusal are occurrence-scoped facts held here; names, addresses and affiliations are not mastered here.
The model classifies openness, marks closed portions and stores references to audit events raised elsewhere. It does not evaluate authorisation, enforce it, or hold the audit trail.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Conferencing platform (XCON model or vendor service)
boundary_notes.distinction: Conference object state, admission policy enforcement, floor control and media handling are the platform's runtime concern. This model binds the conference object identifier, the published endpoints and the exported attendance observations.
iCalendar, JSCalendar and schema.org Event are alignments. Mappings are recorded with their lossy points; no conformance is claimed and no format is required by the semantics.

bundles.name: Session constitution and convening basis
bundles.description: What this occurrence is, how it is identified and classified, and the authority and notice under which it exists.
bundles.rationale: Nothing else about a meeting is interpretable until the occurrence is uniquely identifiable, correctly classified for the procedural regime that applies to it, and traceable to a party entitled to convene it. Statutory open-meeting and company-law regimes attach their obligations to exactly these facts.

bundles.rationale: A session is bounded in time and place, and both the planned and the observed values carry procedural weight. Calendaring standards fix the time and recurrence semantics, conferencing standards fix the access channel, and accessibility guidance fixes the conditions for equivalent participation.

composition.target: WM-ACT-018 — parent activity or occurrence model
composition.purpose: Specialise the generic occurrence with the deliberative surface only: agenda, quorum determination, procedural acts, motions, capture and record obligation. Generic occurrence identity, scheduling status and cancellation semantics remain defined by the parent and are not redefined here.

Carry the obligation to produce a durable record, its required content, producer and certifier references, and the anchor map from items and acts to record passages. The record's draft, approval, correction, authenticity, publication and disposition lifecycle stays with the target. Mandatory where an open-meeting or company-law regime applies; absent otherwise.

Route a declared outcome to a durable decision record and hold the returned reference. Decision rationale, status, supersession and implementation tracking belong to the target; only the conduct of putting and deciding the question is modelled here.

Bind the occurrence to the body that convened it and resolve the quorum threshold, voting entitlement and presiding rules from it at read time. Membership, mandate and delegated powers are not copied into the occurrence.

composition.purpose: Align participant, virtual location, structured participant type and resource semantics; note that JSCalendar excludes participant-only changes from the sequence counter, which the local revision rule mirrors.

Align attendance mode, event status, organiser and attendee roles, superordinate and subordinate event links, and the recordedIn relation used for the durable record link. The postponed and rescheduled statuses have no lossless calendaring equivalent and are recorded as a conflict.

composition.target: OASIS Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0 debate vocabulary
composition.purpose: Align procedural act kinds, roll call, quorum, voting and speech attribution vocabulary. Akoma Ntoso models the debate document rather than the occurrence, so its document-level structures belong to WM-REC-012.

composition.target: IETF RFC 6501 XCON conference information data model
composition.purpose: Align the conference object identifier, admission policy and platform role vocabulary. Conference state, floor control mechanics and media handling remain the platform's runtime concern.

Source governed code lists for participation statuses, participation roles, calendar user types, methods, classifications, participant types, resource types and feature types instead of minting local equivalents.

owner_package_requirements: Name one accountable owner for the Meeting / Session package who can decide classification code lists, approve alignment mappings and sign off breaking changes; the registry entry currently carries only a placeholder owner and must be resolved before the model leaves candidate status.

Declare the authoritative master system for meeting identifiers (typically the secretariat or governance register) and publish the fallback order used when that system has not yet issued an identifier.
Publish the resolved references for the four external dependencies this model cannot function without: the convening body model, the party model, the durable record models and the retention schedule.

Register the local code lists that have no IANA or schema.org equivalent — meeting type, formality class, procedural act kind, voting method, closure ground — with their governing instrument and review cycle.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint occurrence identifiers in a namespace controlled by the adopting Dimension and never inside a vendor calendar's identifier space. Where a globally scoped identifier is published, use a domain-qualified form whose right-hand side is a domain the Dimension controls, so that the identifier stays resolvable when the calendaring or conferencing platform changes. Keep platform-assigned conference object identifiers and attendance report identifiers in a separate bound-identifier map rather than promoting one of them to the primary identifier.
registry_links: IANA iCalendar Element Registries for participation statuses, roles, calendar user types, methods, classifications, participant types, resource types and feature types (https://www.iana.org/assignments/icalendar/icalendar.xhtml)
schema.org type and enumeration registry for event status and attendance mode terms (https://schema.org/Event)
The adopting Dimension's own model registry entry vr.wm-act-025, which records the relations to WM-ORG-018, WM-REC-012 and WM-REC-010 and their review state

canonicalization_rules: Express every instant as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and retain the named scheduling time zone as a separate value, because a local wall-clock recurrence rule cannot be reconstructed from a fixed offset.
Order agenda items by their sequence position as set down, and record the order actually followed as a separate observed sequence rather than by mutating the original ordering.
Normalise governed code values to the registered token in its registered case; unregistered local extensions carry an explicit local prefix so they are never mistaken for registered values.
Canonicalise party references to the master identifier before comparison; display names and calendar addresses are never used as join keys.
Represent presence as half-open intervals with explicit join and leave instants; a missing leave instant is recorded as open rather than defaulted to the session close.
patch_rules: Patches address stable local identifiers, never array positions, so that inserting an agenda item or a procedural act does not invalidate outstanding patches.
Any change by the convener to the definition of the occurrence — start, end, setting, agenda, status — increments the revision sequence and records the change instant and the acting party reference.

Participation status changes, presence observations and attendance corrections do not increment the revision sequence, mirroring the normative calendaring rule that attendee responses are not organiser revisions.
Differences between a series definition and one occurrence are expressed as an instance patch against the series, not by copying the whole definition.

A patch never modifies a referenced target model's record; changes to minutes, decision records, tasks or party data are requested through the owning model and only the returned reference is updated here.
compatibility_rules: Adding a value to a local code list, or adding an optional data element, is a minor change; removing a required element, narrowing a cardinality or changing the identity strategy is breaking.
Changing which system is authoritative for a field is breaking for consumers that rely on the field authority flags, and must be announced with the mapping table it affects.
An alignment mapping may be corrected, but a correction that changes previously emitted projections is recorded as a conflict entry with the affected profile and version, not applied silently.
Deprecated elements remain readable for at least one full retention cycle of the occurrences that use them before removal is proposed.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for meetings in the adopting Dimension — for example the governance secretariat's meeting register identifier or the docket number of the convening body — which always takes precedence when it exists.
Governed global identifier or IRI published for the occurrence, such as a domain-qualified calendaring UID or a Dimension-controlled URI, used when no master-system identifier has been issued.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension as a last resort, retained as an alias once a master-system identifier is later issued so that existing references continue to resolve.

A meeting date, a room booking reference, a position in a series, a conferencing join code or an agenda title is never an identifier; each may be an attribute or a bound external identifier, but none may be promoted to primary identity.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every instant is recorded as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z, and the named scheduling time zone is retained beside it because an offset alone cannot reproduce local wall-clock or daylight-saving behaviour. Event time — when the session actually opened, suspended, resumed, voted or closed — is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time — when a clerk, conferencing platform or importer captured or loaded the value — whenever the two differ, and neither is inferred from the other. Where the offset is genuinely unknown but the instant is known in UTC, the '-00:00' form is used rather than 'Z', preserving the documented distinction.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — notices, agendas, divisions and closure certifications — are numbered within the issuing register or within the occurrence, never across this model as a whole: notices and agendas take the convening body's register series, divisions take a sequential ordinal within the occurrence, and closure certifications take the issuing legal office's series. The serial is a human-facing label; the artifact's identity remains the issuing register's identifier bound to the session identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact is bound to the occurrence by the session identifier plus the revision sequence current at issue, and to the agenda item or portion it concerns where one applies. Where a checksum or signature exists it is recorded with its algorithm name, and captured media additionally record duration and byte length. The model records integrity evidence and its provenance; it does not verify signatures, enforce integrity or hold the audit trail of verification, which belong to the services referenced by the adopting Dimension.

policies: Session context is captured only for the declared purpose of conducting and recording the occurrence; introducing a capture modality beyond those notified to participants requires a fresh notification before capture resumes and, where the applicable regime requires it, a recorded consent basis.

Openness classification is determined before the occurrence opens; moving a portion to a closed classification requires a recorded procedural act, a stated ground drawn from the applicable regime and an identified certifier, and the fact that a closure occurred remains disclosable even when its content does not.

Alignment with external vocabularies is declarative. Conformance is asserted only where a field mapping has been tested and recorded, and every unmappable concept is carried as an explicit loss note rather than dropped.

Personal data held by the occurrence is limited to what the procedural or record obligation requires; presence intervals, contribution attributions and accommodation needs are minimised at capture and carry an explicit necessity statement.
This model records references to decisions, records, tasks and audit events; it never mirrors their state. A stale reference is reported as unresolved rather than resolved from a local copy.

read: A read returns identity, classification, planned timing, openness state and the convening binding by default; participant response detail, presence intervals, contribution attributions and closed-portion content are withheld unless the requester holds the corresponding scope.
A closed occurrence is read in the state it held at close; linked record and decision references are returned as references with their resolution state, never resolved into local copies at read time.
Projections into external vocabularies are read-only derivations that apply the requester's access scope before mapping, so that a projection can never disclose more than a direct read would.
create: An occurrence may be created only with a planned start and a named time zone, an openness class, and either a resolved convening reference or an explicit unattached flag stating that no governance body convened it.
Creation assigns the identifier by the declared identity priority; where a provisional Dimension-assigned identifier is used, it is retained as an alias once the master-system identifier is issued.
Creating an occurrence never creates a minutes, transcript, decision or task record; it may only record that such a record is owed, with its basis and deadline.
update: Convener changes to the definition increment the revision sequence and record the change instant and acting party reference; response, presence and attendance-correction updates do not increment it.
After close, updates are limited to attendance corrections, linkage of produced records and decisions, disposition markers and reconciliation outcomes, each carrying a reason and an actor reference.
An update never rewrites a recorded procedural act, division tally or declared result in place; a correction is recorded as a new entry that supersedes the earlier one and retains it.
delete: Occurrence entries are not hard-deleted while any retention obligation over them is live. The entry is closed, marked non-current and scheduled for disposition against the retention schedule referenced by the adopting Dimension; statutory floors differ by regime (for example a ten-year floor for company meeting records and resolutions, and a two-year floor for closed-meeting transcripts under the United States open-meeting statute), and the strictest applicable floor governs.

Where an occurrence entry must be withdrawn because it was created in error or duplicates another, a tombstone is retained carrying the identifier, its aliases, the withdrawal reason, the withdrawing actor and the withdrawal instant, so that references held by notices, minutes, decision records and calendar copies do not dangle.

Disposal of the minutes or transcript is executed under WM-REC-012, and disposal of decision records under WM-REC-010. This model neither performs nor authorises those disposals; it records the reference, its resolution state and the disposal outcome reported back to it.

Erasure or restriction of participant personal data held by the occurrence — presence intervals, calendar addresses, accommodation requests and capture media — is executed by the adopting Dimension's data-protection policy owner and its designated processor. This model records the disposition due instant, the request and the returned outcome reference, not the erasure operation itself.

Capture media held by a conferencing platform expire under that platform's own retention policy; where the occurrence owes a longer-lived record, the export obligation and its deadline are recorded here and the exported copy's custodian reference is bound before the source window closes.

roles.name: Model owner
responsibilities: Decide and publish the local code lists, the identity priority and the authoritative master system for meeting identifiers
Approve alignment mappings and record conflicts rather than resolving them silently
Sign off breaking changes and their migration path

roles.name: Session secretariat or clerk
responsibilities: Create the occurrence, issue notice within the required lead time and circulate accessible agenda materials
Maintain the attendance register, quorum determinations, procedural act sequence and division records during the occurrence
Commission the durable records owed and bind the returned references and anchor maps

roles.name: Presiding officer
responsibilities: Declare procedural acts, rule on objections and declare voting results
Determine and certify the closure of portions on a stated ground where the regime permits it
Confirm the accuracy of the attendance and division records for which the applicable regime requires certification

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Maintain and test the field mappings to calendaring, event and conferencing vocabularies and record every lossy point
Maintain the bound external identifier map and the field authority flags between platform and local copies
Trigger export obligations before a platform's source retention window closes

roles.name: Data protection and records liaison
responsibilities: Maintain the personal data inventory, necessity statements and processing bases for occurrence-held data
Resolve the applicable retention floors and record disposition due instants and returned outcome references
Route erasure, restriction and disposal requests to the owning policy and record models rather than executing them here

access.default_rule: Deny by default. A caller reaches an occurrence only through an explicitly granted scope, and the openness class together with any closed-portion markers further restricts the field set returned; where no explicit determination exists, the more restrictive of the meeting type's default and the requester's scope applies.
exceptions: Where a statutory open-meeting regime applies, the notice fields, agenda, openness status and the fact that a portion was closed are readable without authentication, even though the closed portion's content is not.
A participant may always read their own participation record: their role, invitation status, delegation state, presence intervals and any accommodation request they submitted.
Closed-portion content is restricted to parties recorded as present for that portion, plus the certifying officer and the record producer named for it.
Accessibility accommodation data is restricted to the accommodation coordinator and the requesting participant, and is excluded from every general attendance projection.
A legal hold or live proceeding suspends disposition and re-opens read access for the designated custodian even where a disposition due instant has passed.
Capture media are readable only under an explicit media scope that is separate from the scope granting access to the occurrence itself.
audit_requirements: Every read of closed-portion content and every export of capture media, presence data or attendance reports must be recorded by the adopting Dimension's audit service; this model stores only the returned audit event reference and never the trail itself.

Changes to the openness class, to a closure ground, to the certified attendance register and to a recorded division must be attributable to an acting party reference and an event instant recorded separately from the ingestion instant.
Access decisions are evaluated and enforced by the referenced access-policy service; this model records the classification inputs and the decision reference, and asserts no enforcement of its own.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name, Type, Model ID and Registry ID before touching any occurrence data.
Follow the Specification URL to obtain the bundle, layer and finding structure, the identity priority and the timestamp rule.
Follow the Storage type URL to learn the projection in use — file tree, document store, graph or version-controlled text — remembering that the projection is not the semantics.
Follow the Interface URL to learn the read, create, update and delete surface and the scope names required for each.
Follow the Processes URL to learn the convening, agenda, invitation, quorum, voting, closure and record hand-off procedures and their preconditions.
Resolve the referenced convening body, party, record and retention models before writing; if any is unresolved, create only the unattached-flagged form and report the gap.
Consult the Alignment conflicts URL before emitting any external projection, so that recorded conflicts are carried as loss notes rather than resolved locally.

coverage.claim: Claude-only coverage of one convened meeting or session occurrence — identity and classification, convening authority and notice, planned and observed timing, series position, physical and virtual setting, accessibility, participation, presence and quorum, agenda composition and conduct, motions and voting, in-session capture, record obligation, openness and interchange — across 6 bundles, 12 layers, 25 findings, 103 questions, 12 artifacts and 10 functions, grounded in 15 sources (IETF calendaring/conferencing, IANA registries, OASIS Akoma Ntoso, schema.org Event, one W3C Group Note, UK company law and two LII reproductions of US federal open-meeting statute). Coverage is partial by construction and by audit: durable records (WM-REC-012, WM-REC-010), the convening body (WM-ORG-018), party/place/document/task masters and access-evaluation and audit services are referenced rather than owned; meeting-level security controls are an admitted gap; and the retention, access, temporal and identity checklist dimensions are over-claimed relative to the questions the structure actually carries and are downgraded by this audit. Sources were not verified live during this audit and no independent second-provider review exists. No universal completeness is claimed.

checklist.notes: Occurrence identity, series and recurrence discrimination, revision sequence and bound external identifiers are grounded in RFC 5545, RFC 8984 and RFC 6501; the identity priority puts the master-system identifier first and explicitly excludes dates, join codes and series positions.

Convocation, adoption of agenda, opening, suspension, resumption, closure of portions, adjournment, cancellation and post-close correction are modelled as occurrence states and typed acts. The lifecycles of the minutes and decision records are deliberately excluded and referenced.

Links to the convening body, parent activity model, record models, party, place, document and task models are declared as composition entries with an explicit ownership boundary in each purpose statement.

Planned versus observed times, named scheduling time zone retained beside the offset, suspension intervals, presence intervals, recurrence position and deadline anchoring are all modelled; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is required and event time is separated from observation time.

Observation source and observing actor for presence, contribution attribution with speaking capacity, declaring officer for every procedural act, originating product for revisions, and platform-versus-local field authority flags.

Convening authority binding, presiding officer for the occurrence, item sponsorship, action assignee, record producer and certifier are each held as references with an occurrence-scoped meaning; standing mandates remain with the governance body model.

Quorum determination against an externally owned threshold, notice sufficiency and defect handling, presence source reconciliation, cross-copy reconciliation by revision and timestamp, and outcome evidence questions.

Openness classification, closed-portion grounds and certification, observer admission and exclusion, embargo, plus a deny-by-default service rule with named exceptions. Evaluation and enforcement are explicitly delegated.

Disposition due instants, the strictest-applicable-floor rule with two divergent statutory examples, tombstones for withdrawn entries, platform export obligations before source expiry, and explicit statements that the record models and the Dimension's data-protection policy execute disposal.

Declarative alignment to iCalendar, iTIP, JSCalendar, RFC 9073, schema.org, Akoma Ntoso and XCON, with a field mapping table, loss notes for unmappable concepts and recorded conflicts instead of asserted conformance.

Accommodation capture, provided services, advance circulation deadlines in accessible native formats and caption or interpretation quality assessment, grounded in the W3C remote-meetings note; the note is a Group Note, not a Recommendation, so it is treated as guidance rather than a normative requirement.

Capture notification and consent basis, personal data inventory with necessity statements, sensitivity flags and consent-withdrawal handling. No jurisdiction-specific lawfulness determination is made by the model.
Motion, voting method, threshold, tally, exclusions and result declaration are modelled as session conduct, with routing to WM-REC-010 for the durable decision.
Presence counts and intervals, participant totals, observed item durations, division tallies and observed procedural timings, each carrying its observation source.

Deliberately not owned. The model records classification inputs and audit event references; the trail itself and its retention belong to the adopting Dimension's audit service, in line with the reference-not-ownership rule.

Moderator credentials are held as a pointer to an external secret store and channel restriction is modelled, but no primary source was found for a governed vocabulary of meeting-level security controls such as lobby policy, watermarking or exfiltration limits. Marked as a gap rather than presented as canonical.

known_omissions: Multilingual regimes beyond the fact that interpretation was provided: language coverage per speaker, booth assignment and relay chains are not modelled.
Floor control protocol mechanics, media negotiation and codec selection; only the floor control policy code and the resulting speaking turns are held.
Cost, travel, catering and logistics of convening a meeting.
Hearing and tribunal specifics — oath administration, witness examination sequence, exhibits and evidentiary rulings — are only partially reachable through the generic procedural act vocabulary.
Machine-evaluable encoding of standing orders, so that a rule such as a casting-vote entitlement can be checked automatically rather than recorded as text.
Decisions taken without a meeting (written resolutions, silence procedure) are excluded by definition and need a sibling model if the adopting Dimension transacts business that way.
Anonymous or unregistered public attendance at large open meetings, where a per-party presence record cannot be produced.
conflicts: Status vocabularies diverge: iCalendar STATUS offers only TENTATIVE, CONFIRMED and CANCELLED, while schema.org adds EventPostponed, EventRescheduled and EventMovedOnline. Postponement and rescheduling therefore have no lossless calendaring equivalent and must be carried as a loss note plus a superseding-occurrence reference.

Three incompatible role vocabularies exist: iCalendar ROLE (CHAIR, REQ-PARTICIPANT, OPT-PARTICIPANT, NON-PARTICIPANT), JSCalendar roles (owner, attendee, optional, informational, chair, multi-valued) and XCON roles (administrator, moderator, participant). No normative crosswalk between them was found; the mapping is recorded as a conflict rather than asserted.

Identifier spaces do not compose: an iCalendar UID, an XCON conference object URI and a vendor meeting identifier are independent namespaces with no normative binding, which is why the model keeps a bound-identifier map with authority flags instead of promoting one to primary identity.

Statutory retention floors conflict across jurisdictions: UK company law requires records of resolutions and meetings to be kept for at least ten years, while the United States open-meeting statute requires closed-meeting transcripts, recordings or minutes for at least two years, or one year after the related proceeding ends, whichever is later. A platform default such as a one-year attendance report retention may be shorter than both.

The statutory definition of a meeting is narrower than the calendaring one: an open-meeting statute defines a meeting as deliberation by the number of members required to take action that determines official business, whereas any calendaring event with attendees qualifies structurally. Classification therefore cannot be derived from structure alone.

Revision semantics are not a plain version counter: the organiser controls the sequence, participant responses must not increment it, and where sequences tie the message timestamp decides. Systems that treat the counter as a generic optimistic-lock version will diverge.

Akoma Ntoso models the debate document rather than the session entity, so its vocabulary supports procedural act and speech classification here but its document structures belong to the minutes model. Treating it as a session schema would duplicate WM-REC-012.
regional_assumptions: Recording legality varies by jurisdiction, including between all-party and one-party consent regimes. The model records a consent basis and notification facts but makes no legality determination.

The open-meeting obligations, closure exemptions and minute-content requirements cited are United States federal; equivalent regimes in other jurisdictions differ in the closure grounds, the certification role and the retention floor.
The ten-year retention floor for meeting records is drawn from UK company law and applies to companies constituted under it, not to public bodies or to other jurisdictions.
Quorum, proxy, casting-vote and written-resolution rules are entity-type and jurisdiction specific and are always resolved from the convening body's instrument rather than defaulted here.

Time handling assumes proleptic Gregorian dates and IANA time zone identifiers; non-Gregorian recurrence and jurisdictions with irregular daylight-saving changes need the named zone retained, which is why an offset alone is not accepted.
Platform retention windows and export behaviour are vendor and tenancy specific; the one-year attendance report window cited is one vendor's documented policy, not a general rule.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a normative crosswalk between iCalendar ROLE, JSCalendar roles and XCON roles and found none; recorded it as a conflict rather than inventing a mapping and presenting it as canonical.

Tested whether approval of the minutes belongs to this model. It does not: approval appears here only as an agenda item of a later occurrence, while the approval state of the record is owned by WM-REC-012. The record-production finding was rewritten to hold obligation and linkage only.

Tested whether quorum rules should be local. Rejected: the threshold is a property of the convening body's constitution, so only the determination event, its counted base and its outcome are held here.

Tested whether an audit trail of who viewed a closed session belongs here. Rejected under the reference-not-ownership rule; the model stores audit event references and classification inputs, and the checklist marks audit trail as not-applicable rather than covered.

Checked counterexamples that stress the definition: asynchronous written procedures (excluded, no occurrence exists), always-on standing conference bridges (excluded until a convened occurrence is declared on them) and one-to-one calls (in scope structurally but usually carrying no agenda, quorum or record obligation).

Verified that no declared artifact duplicates the minutes, transcript or decision record; the twelve artifacts are notices, agendas, registers, platform exports, speaker lists, division records, action lists, capture media, scheduling messages, accommodation requests and closure certifications.

Checked whether the interchange finding should declare a projection artifact. Rejected, because treating a format projection as an artifact would contradict the requirement that the model remain independent of storage format and interface; the only exchanged document declared is the scheduling message.

Re-read every bundle, layer, finding and function against the three known-relation rationales and moved decision rationale, record approval, body membership and task execution out to composition links, out_of_scope entries or boundary notes.
